questions.question: What should be decided before an application stores a value in Redis?
options: Only the shortest possible key name
The value's authority, freshness, durability, and placement contract
A universal one-hour TTL
Whether every command can run on every cluster node
questions.explanation: Redis can be a disposable cache, durable state store, coordination aid, or event system. Correctness depends on making authority, staleness, loss tolerance, and placement explicit for each key family.

questions.question: What is the safest invariant for data stored in Memcached?
options: Every cached value is automatically replicated to another node
The application can reconstruct or refetch the value after a miss or eviction
A zero TTL makes the value durable
The cache is the authoritative transaction log
questions.explanation: Memcached is a disposable acceleration layer. The durable source and application miss path must be able to reconstruct every cached value.

questions.question: What is the safest statement about an indexed document and search visibility?
options: A successful source-database commit guarantees immediate Elasticsearch visibility
The document becomes searchable when its indexed representation is exposed by refresh
A replica makes the document searchable before the primary applies it
A snapshot controls when the document appears in search
questions.explanation: Indexing acceptance and search visibility are separate moments. Refresh publishes searchable Lucene segments; source commits, replica count, and snapshots do not eliminate that boundary.

questions.question: A product title must support full-text search, phrase matching, alphabetical sorting, and display in results. Which field design covers all four behaviors?
options: StoredField only
StringField only
TextField with storage plus a normalized SortedDocValuesField
TextField without storage
questions.explanation: TextField creates the analyzed postings and positions, storage returns the original title, and sorted doc values provide a per-document ordering value.

questions.question: What identifies an object in a typical object store?
options: A bucket or container plus an object key and, when versioned, a version identifier
A mutable filesystem inode only
A database row lock
A TCP connection
questions.explanation: Object APIs address immutable or replaceable values through a namespace and key, with version identity where enabled.

questions.question: A peak sends 80,000 viewer requests per second and the edge hit rate is 90%. Before considering another cache layer, how many requests per second remain on the miss path?
questions.explanation: Ten percent of 80,000 is 8,000. The origin path must be planned from absolute misses, not the hit-rate percentage alone.
